items.title: Joseph Ralph Robinson Interview, 1960-10-12
items.q: I bought it from a fella named, uh, Fair Charles.

ctx.x: Well, you'd be just young though then. Yeah, I was a young fella. How old would you be when you took up the violin? Well...

You said eighteen, you told me yesterday, you bought the violin. Yeah, eighteen, I bought the violin. Had you played before that? From a fella, that violin you took, you got there. Yeah. I bought it from a fella named, uh, Fair Charles. In a place they call Livonia, Louisiana. Livonia. We had a railroad, uh, we had a railroad, uh, stage. He had a stool just on this side, the railroad, you know. Yeah. And I used to go there, he had two. And so, I asked him once. I had one, I had a violin myself, you know. Yeah.…
When you took up the clarinet, you say you just played by ear? You didn't live?
